authority_boundary.owner_basis: The Product Owner ratified Q1 through Q6 as proposed. This record materializes Q3 only and applies Q2 and Q4 exactly.
authority_boundary.permitted_effect: May be hash-bound by the five fresh zero-contribution concurrence receipts as evidence for a later owner decision.
not_authorized: F2 restart, repair, commit, push, or workflow
editing accepted F1 bytes or the stopped uncommitted F2 draft
adding, removing, renumbering, or changing valid semantics of any official MCP vector
adapter-dependent mapping subject-digest or authenticated mapping collision qualification

closed_fixture_semantics.one_id_one_leaf: Each canonical fixture ID below identifies exactly one executable scenario. Ranges and prose bundles are expanded; an alias never creates a second fixture.
closed_fixture_semantics.input: The named request or protected-record input is encoded in its unique canonical spelling at the stated boundary values. A negative input changes only the field named by that leaf.
closed_fixture_semantics.schedule: Steps are ordered left to right. A named crash occurs after the preceding durable or physical step and before the following step, followed by a process restart when stated.
closed_fixture_semantics.expected: The implementation fixture must freeze exact canonical response or six-field canonical error-envelope bytes and the durable/physical post-state described by the leaf. No message, details, raw secret, raw path, SQL, stack, exception text, or external subject may appear.
closed_fixture_semantics.mutation: zero means no authority row, event, anchor, file, secret-reveal, idempotency-result, or success-activity mutation. A named allowed mutation is exhaustive; every unnamed mutation is forbidden.
closed_fixture_semantics.closed_error_projection: Where a leaf names CURSOR_STALE, it projects to GKOS_P6_REQUEST_STALE_AUTHORITY. Invalid canonical/schema inputs project to GKOS_P6_INVALID_PARAMS unless the leaf names a narrower existing code. No new error code is introduced.
